items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: And then I started seeing Ruby Keeler and Dick Powell and those movies

ctx.x: Did you — were you turned on by the Swing Era music, and then the jazz that was being played at the time?

No. It’s all because of my father had a 78, a Decca 78 album of “The Jolson Story” with two pictures of white gloves on the cover. No picture of Jolson or anything like that. And I fell in love with his voice and phrasing. Now I was a strange kid, I mean I’m four years old and this is 1962 and I loved these records. And I used to imitate them, it was kind of strange for a little kid. And that got me into, I mean I was already kind of like — you know I should tie up the Jolson thread just for a moment, that the…

sudden I got this bug about oh boy, well all that other stuff was great but boy there’s something about that that really gets me. Well my local public library had a copy of Benny Goodman’s 1938 Carnegie Hall concert, a double LP, which influenced so many people of a certain age. And I fell in love with it. And I just loved listening to it. And at that point I had been taking — I started piano lessons when I was 4. And you know, a typical thing, an old lady who lived on my little street who had like a living room…
